title: What Stalin Really Thought About Hitler
the_thought: He thought if he was nice to a bad man, the bad man would leave him alone.
hook: He thought if he was nice to a bad man, the bad man would leave him alone.

levels.name: The Toast
beats: That is the whole idea. Say it again so it sticks. Be nice. Share. Smile. And the scary man will go hurt someone else. Two in the morning, they sign a paper. He lifts a glass and drinks to the other man's health. The room smiles. Photographers take pictures. He is smiling because he thinks the paper worked.

Worked, in his head, means this. The other man will now go fight far away. Not here. A smile and a signature, he thinks, can turn a bad man into a helper. That is a child's deal. He ran a country on it.

levels.name: The Line
beats: Why does he need a helper? Because he is scared. He already hurt his own army. He shot the men who knew how to fight. So he needs time. He needs the fire to stay in someone else's house, not his.

So he draws a line on a map. You take that side. He takes this side. Nobody hits anybody. Then he puts the paper in a drawer, like putting a toy away and saying we are done. He sends food the other way. Grain on trains. Steel coming back. He even sends a birthday wish. Happy birthday. You don't say happy birthday to a man you believe will burn your house. You say it to a man you think you've made safe.

levels.name: The Cellar
beats: He sends a helper to talk about oil and land. Bombs fall. They have to finish talking in a basement. Friends do not make you hide underground. That should have been enough.
People try to warn him anyway. A spy. A letter. Lights in the trees at night. He hears them. Then he says no. Nothing is coming. Those people are lying. Nine days later the lights are tanks.

He says no because the simple idea has to stay true. If the bad man was never going to listen, then the smile was a mistake, and the food was a mistake, and the birthday was a mistake. So he lets the army sleep. The last train of food still goes out after dark.

levels.name: The Phone
beats: June. A Sunday. Still dark. The phone rings. His soldier says the border is broken. Planes. Fire. The bad man did not send a letter. He sent an army.

At first he says maybe it is only a trick. A trick you can talk about. An army you cannot. Then he understands the simple idea was wrong. He leaves the city. He sits in a little house in the trees and will not answer the phone. For days. The most powerful man in the country, hiding, because the story he told himself broke.
He smiled. He drew the line. He sent the birthday. And when the bad man came into his house anyway, he had no other story left.

levels.name: The Dust
beats: He comes back because the fire does not wait. Later he will make speeches. The true thought is this morning. He believed a piece of paper could make a bad man good.
A lot of people died. That is what happens when you feed someone who already said he was hungry for your house. He thought he had bought safety. He had only bought time for the other man.
Last picture. The little house. The glass from the toast, empty, with dust in it. He drank with the man. He never understood him.
Say it like a child one more time. He thought if he was nice to a bad man, the bad man would leave him alone. The bad man did not.
